name: Cataract surgery
summary: How expats navigate cataract assessment and surgery in Singapore — public vs private pathways, lens options, and why optical shops cannot replace ophthalmology surgical counselling.
body:
Cataracts are a common reason older expats and ageing parents on LTVP suddenly struggle with night driving, glare, and reading. Surgery is highly standardised and effective — shopping should focus on surgeon pathway and aftercare, not only “laser cataract” ads.

## Pathway
- Ophthalmology exam with dilated lens assessment
- Biometry for intraocular lens (IOL) power
- Discussion of monofocal vs toric vs multifocal/EDOF options and trade-offs
- Day surgery and post-op drop regimens
- Second-eye timing decisions

Optical refraction alone cannot time surgery; opaque lens changes need an ophthalmologist.

## Cost and insurance
Public pathways can be excellent with different waiting and fee structures by residency status. Private centres offer faster scheduling and premium IOL menus — get itemised quotes (surgeon, facility, lens, anaesthetist). Many medical plans cover medically necessary cataract surgery with sub-limits; refractive lens exchange marketed to younger patients is a different product.

## How to choose
Prefer ophthalmologists who explain glare/contrast trade-offs of multifocal lenses in humid, high-glare Singapore driving — not only “never need glasses again.” Ask about posterior capsule opacification YAG rates and emergency contact after hours. Bring prior spectacle prescriptions and any macular history.

## Practical tip
Arrange a companion for the first post-op day and avoid swimming/eye makeup for the advised window. If Mum is visiting on a short pass, confirm enough days on-island for reviews before she flies.
